newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel sees 1997 as tough on sales, profit.
newsitem.headline: Opel sees 1997 as tough on sales, profit.

text.p: Adam Opel AG, the German unit of General Motors Corp., said Thursday that its 1996 sales rose 9.3 percent to 28 billion marks ($17 billion) but it expected weaker profits for the year due to competition.
Opel said its 1996 profit would be at the high end of a range between 250 million and 350 million marks but below the 1995 level of 363 million marks.
"We are satisfied with the results when viewed against the background of stiff competition and difficult industry conditions in 1996," Opel Chief Executive David Herman said.
Herman warned, however, of ongoing tough times for 1997, saying Opel expected a lower rate of market growth.
He also said the company faces pressure on sales, profit and vehicle deliveries due to growing competition from importers, particularly from South Korea.
But Opel said it would seek to expand its production and customer base despite tough times by teaming up with French carmaker Renault to build a series of light trucks.
The move marks Opel's return to a European market segment it had abandoned 20 years ago and that has since been dominated by rivals Volkswagen AG and Ford Motor Corp .
"It has been time for years to climb back into this market," Herman said.
Opel also said it was reviewing a potential joint venture with Suzuki Motor Corp. of Japan to produce small cars but a deal has not yet been finalised.
